headline: High: aci can egress CRM/email data into pdf.js browser-based processing, creating default-path leakage and cascading trust risks; prompt-injection risk is lower because the pair lacks a direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can use MCP/direct function calls and pdf.js runs browser-based tests, but the profiles do not show a default shared channel or that pdf.js ingests aci output as instructions. The plausible bridge is manual or orchestrated file handoff, so injection is possible but not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies aci output into a PDF or browser test fixture that pdf.js parses as trusted text, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared MCP server or clipboard bridge is added between the agents, prompt content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable any automatic copy/paste or file relay between agents.
Require a human review step before pdf.js consumes aci-generated text.
Use separate workspaces for aci and pdf.js.
Add provenance labels to any transferred content.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering on the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; pdf.js processes PDF files locally with no egress. If aci exports sensitive records into PDFs or attachments that pdf.js opens in the same workspace, sensitive data can flow across the pair in default-ish workflows, though pdf.js itself is not a transmitter.
conditions: IF aci writes CRM or email content into PDFs that pdf.js opens, the same data class crosses agents.
IF both agents share a filesystem or download directory, PDF contents can be exposed to pdf.js.
mitigations: Keep aci and pdf.js on separate directories.
Block aci from exporting sensitive fields into PDFs.
Open PDFs only from a quarantined folder.
Turn off any automatic upload or sync from the PDF workspace.
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before file handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, but aci’s write surface is API-based integrations while pdf.js is file-only and network-egress-free. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources like the same filesystem or git state, so direct write conflict is not evidenced; uncertainty stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory or shared document store, write contention can occur.
IF aci is configured to update the same CRM record set that pdf.js-derived workflows also modify, conflicts increase.
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same folder or record set.
Serialize updates through one operator.
Use read-only access for pdf.js.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar outputs that may be treated as authoritative by downstream workflows, while pdf.js is a document processor that can render or extract from those outputs. The pair lacks a built-in verification step, so errors from aci can cascade into pdf.js-driven decisions or documents.
conditions: IF pdf.js consumes aci-generated documents without human verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF aci output is used as source text for PDFs or browser tests, downstream rendering can amplify mistakes.
mitigations: Require human review of aci outputs before PDF generation.
Add a validation checklist for extracted facts.
Mark aci-generated content as untrusted.
Compare against source records before acting.
requires-engineering: implement automated provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, support, and calendar data with broad egress, while pdf.js processes PDF documents locally and is verified open-source. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but if regulated customer data is exported from aci into PDFs for pdf.js processing, retention and subject-rights controls can diverge.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from aci is written into PDFs processed by pdf.js, retention and access controls must align.
IF the deployment stores PDFs longer than the source CRM records, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Minimize regulated fields in exported PDFs.
Set a short retention window for PDF artifacts.
Keep an audit log of file transfers.
Restrict PDF access to the same role set as CRM data.
requires-engineering: map residency and retention policies end-to-end.
